market_context: United States/international; opened refrigerated commercial hummus and homemade hummus.
title: How Long Does Opened Hummus Last in the Refrigerator?

seo.title: How Long Does Opened Hummus Last in the Fridge?
seo.meta_description: A useful household reference for opened commercial hummus is about 7 days refrigerated at 40°F or below, unless the label gives a shorter time. Homemade hummus deserves a more conservative window. Keep utensils clean and limit time at room temperature.
seo.search_intent: Understand how many days opened hummus keeps, how commercial and homemade hummus differ, how to store it, and what signs mean it should be discarded.

excerpt: Opened commercial pasteurized hummus is commonly given a refrigerator window of about 7 days at 40 °F (4 °C) or below, unless the manufacturer gives a shorter after-opening instruction. Homemade or preservative-free hummus deserves a more conservative approach. Clean utensils and limiting room-temperature exposure matter as much as the calendar.
content_html:
For opened refrigerated commercial hummus, about 7 days at 40 °F (4 °C) or below is a useful household reference when the manufacturer does not give a shorter time. USDA FoodKeeper lists roughly one week after opening for commercial pasteurized hummus.

That does not mean every hummus formula lasts exactly the same number of days. Acidity, heat treatment, preservatives, packaging, and contamination during serving all affect shelf life.

The package directions take priority

Some containers say to consume within three days of opening, others five or seven. That instruction is tailored to the specific formula and process.

The unopened sell-by, use-by, or best-quality date is not the same as an after-opening window. Opening adds oxygen and opportunities for contamination from spoons, bread, fingers, or vegetables repeatedly dipped into the container.

If the label gives a shorter window than general storage guidance, follow the label.

Homemade hummus deserves a more conservative window

Homemade hummus usually does not receive the same heat treatment, hygienic filling, or packaging controls as a commercial product. Lemon, salt, and tahini amounts also vary widely.

Prepare an amount you can eat within a few days and keep it continuously refrigerated. Roughly 3–4 days is a prudent household target for homemade hummus, particularly after it has been served several times.

Adding extra lemon later is not a reliable preservation method because final acidity would need to be measured to know its microbiological effect.

Store it cold and avoid recontamination

Keep the refrigerator at 40 °F or below and close the container tightly. Take out only the portion you need and return the rest to refrigeration promptly.

Use clean utensils. Dipping bitten bread, used vegetables, or dirty spoons into the main container can introduce microbes and shorten storage life substantially.

A middle refrigerator shelf is generally more temperature-stable than the door.

Do not leave hummus out for hours

Hummus is a moist ready-to-eat food. General food-safety guidance says perishable foods should be refrigerated within two hours, or one hour when ambient temperature is above 90 °F (32 °C).

A bowl left on a party table all afternoon should not simply be scraped back into the original tub and given another week.

Refrigeration slows microbial growth; it does not reverse growth that already happened while the food was warm.

What spoilage signs matter?

Visible mold, a clearly fermented or unpleasant odor, gas, a swollen package, or unusual sliminess are reasons to discard hummus.

A little oil separation can be normal and does not prove spoilage. Stirring can reincorporate it if the food is still within its expected storage window and has no other warning signs.

Do not taste questionable hummus to determine safety. Some pathogens do not create obvious odor or flavor changes.

Freeze a portion before it gets old

If the hummus is still fresh but you know you will not finish it, freezing a portion is an option. Texture may be less creamy after thawing, but it avoids stretching refrigerator storage too far.

Freeze it earlier in its refrigerated life rather than on the final day. Thaw in the refrigerator and use promptly.

The practical rule: think about one week for opened commercial hummus when the label allows it and refrigeration has been reliable; use a shorter window for homemade hummus. Temperature, clean utensils, and time out of the fridge matter just as much as the day count.

faq.question: How many days does opened commercial hummus last?
faq.answer: USDA FoodKeeper uses about 7 days refrigerated for commercial pasteurized hummus unless the package gives a shorter window.

faq.question: How long does homemade hummus last?
faq.answer: A more conservative target is appropriate; roughly 3–4 refrigerated days is a prudent household window.

faq.question: Is oil separation a sign hummus is bad?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Oil can separate normally. Mold, abnormal odor, gas, swelling, or unusual sliminess are more concerning.
